primary_purpose: Absolute lower-body strength; force production that transfers to sprint/cut speed
cue: Brace the core by breathing into the belly. Drive the knees out as you lower down. Exhale on the way back up.

primary_purpose: Squat pattern competency for novices; equipment-limited substitute
cue: Same bracing/knee-out cue as back squat, at a lighter, more controllable load.

primary_purpose: Movement competency, warm-up, no-equipment option
cue: Brace the core. Drive the knees out.

primary_purpose: Posterior chain strength; hamstring/glute force for sprinting and cutting
cue: Brace the core. Drive the hips back. Stretch the glutes and hamstrings. Stay balanced on the feet.

primary_purpose: Hinge competency, hamstring loading, equipment-limited substitute
cue: Same hinge cue as trap bar deadlift, controlled tempo.

primary_purpose: Single-leg strength; addresses deep lunge mobility demand
cue: Step out and land soft — front knee tracks over the toes, back knee drops straight down like you're kneeling on a pillow. Push the front foot into the ground to stand back up.
notes: Fill in — cue, equipment, regression, progression

primary_purpose: Frontal-plane strength for cutting and marking positions
cue: Sit back into the moving leg, knee over the ankle, and keep the trail leg long and straight. Push off the ground to reset back to center — don't just fall back.

primary_purpose: Throwing-adjacent upper-body power; leg-drive-assisted overhead power
cue: Dip, drive, and punch through the bar — legs start it, arms finish it. Full lockout overhead, ribs stay stacked over your hips, not flared out.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pressing strength; general upper-body power transfer
cue: Set your shoulder blades back and down before you unrack. Bar touches the chest under control, then drive it straight up — push the bar, not just your arms.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pressing strength; equipment-limited substitute, unilateral stability option
cue: Elbows at about 45 degrees, not flared out to the sides. Lower under control, press up and slightly in until the dumbbells nearly touch overhead.

primary_purpose: Vertical pressing strength; shoulder stability for throwing
cue: Brace the core hard before you press — this isn't just a shoulder exercise, it's a full-body one. Press straight up, and get your head through at the top.

primary_purpose: Vertical pressing strength; equipment-limited, unilateral option
cue: Brace like you're about to get hit, then press straight overhead — don't let your lower back arch to get the weight up.

primary_purpose: Upper-chest/shoulder pressing strength, throwing-adjacent
cue: Same press, different angle — this one hits the upper chest, so keep the bench angle moderate and press up and slightly back, not straight up.

primary_purpose: Bodyweight pressing competency; no-equipment option
cue: Straight line from head to heels — squeeze the glutes so the hips don't sag. Chest to the floor, then push the ground away hard.

primary_purpose: Shoulder-friendly pressing angle; unilateral option
cue: Brace, then press the bar up and slightly forward along its natural arc. Keep the ribs down — don't let this turn into a back-extension exercise.

primary_purpose: Triceps/chest pressing strength
cue: Lean forward slightly, elbows tucked, lower under control until you feel a stretch in the shoulders — then press back up without flaring the elbows out.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pulling strength; shoulder health/balance for throwing volume
cue: Hinge at the hips, flat back, and pull the bar to your lower ribs — lead with the elbows, squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.

primary_purpose: Horizontal pulling strength; equipment-limited, unilateral option
cue: Brace through the core so your torso doesn't rotate with the pull. Row the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close to the body, squeeze at the top.

primary_purpose: Vertical pulling strength; upper-body pulling capacity for contested catches/marking
cue: Start from a dead hang, shoulders engaged before you pull. Drive the elbows down and back, chin over the bar, and control the way down — don't just drop.

primary_purpose: Vertical pulling strength; equipment-limited substitute for pull-up
cue: Pull your shoulder blades down and back first, then bring the bar to your upper chest — think elbows to your back pockets, not just hands to the bar.

primary_purpose: Bodyweight horizontal pulling; no/low-equipment option
cue: Body in a straight line, chest to the bar, elbows pulling back and down. The more horizontal your body, the harder it gets — own your angle.

primary_purpose: Scapular health/posture; shoulder-health accessory for throwing volume
cue: Pull the band apart at chest height, squeezing the shoulder blades together like you're pinching a pencil between them. Slow and controlled — this one's about quality, not weight.

primary_purpose: Rear delt/rotator cuff health; shoulder health for throwing volume
cue: Pull to your face, not your chest — elbows high, hands finishing outside your ears like you're flexing. This is where we build shoulder health, not ego.

primary_purpose: Full-body explosive power (triple extension); converts strength into speed/jump ability
cue: Pull the slack out of the bar first — patient off the floor, then explode as it passes the knee. Extend tall through the hips, then get under it fast.

primary_purpose: Simplified pulling position; lower technical demand than full clean
cue: Set from the hang position, hips back, bar against the thighs. Snap the hips forward hard and violently, then get under the bar — this is the whole point of the lift, so attack it.

primary_purpose: Equipment-limited, lower-technical-demand entry point to the clean pattern
cue: Same hip snap as the barbell version, just with dumbbells in your hands — explode the hips, shrug hard, and catch it soft in the front rack.

primary_purpose: Full-body explosive power with overhead stability demand
cue: Same aggressive hip extension as the clean, but this time you're punching the bar straight overhead and dropping under it — commit to the catch, don't second-guess it.

primary_purpose: Simplified snatch entry point
cue: From the hang, snap the hips through violently and pull yourself under the bar fast — overhead lockout should feel active, not passive.

primary_purpose: Builds pulling power without the catch-phase technical demand
cue: This is all about the finish — pull the bar close, extend tall through the hips, shoulders shrugging at the very top. No catch, just pure extension.

primary_purpose: Explosive overhead power via leg drive
cue: Dip straight down, drive straight up, and punch the bar to lockout as you drop under it slightly. Legs do the work — don't try to press it with your arms.

primary_purpose: Hip-hinge-based explosive power; lowest-technical-demand entry to ballistic hip extension
cue: Hinge and hike the bell back between your legs, then snap the hips forward hard to float the weight up — the arms are just along for the ride.

primary_purpose: Rotational core control for throwing
cue: Brace like someone's about to poke you in the stomach, then press the band straight out and resist it pulling your torso around. If your hips rotate, you've lost the rep.

primary_purpose: Converts rotational strength into throwing-specific power
cue: Load into your back hip, then whip the ball across your body into the wall — this should feel explosive, like you're throwing a punch with your whole torso.

primary_purpose: Foundational trunk stability for layout and throwing mechanics
cue: Squeeze the glutes, brace the abs, and keep a dead straight line from shoulders to heels. If your hips sag or pike up, reset.

primary_purpose: Novice-friendly anti-extension core control
cue: Brace the core flat into the floor — no arch in the low back. Lower the opposite arm and leg slow and controlled, then bring them back without losing the brace.

primary_purpose: Advanced anti-extension core strength
cue: Brace hard before you roll out — only go as far as you can keep your low back from arching. Pull back in with the abs, not the arms.

primary_purpose: Hip/oblique control relevant to cutting and marking
cue: Stack your shoulders and hips, and lift through the waist — don't let the hips sag toward the floor. Hold it like you mean it.

primary_purpose: Anti-lateral flexion under asymmetric load
cue: Stand tall, brace hard, and don't let the weight pull you over to one side — walk with control, not a lean.

primary_purpose: Total-body loaded carry; grip and trunk stability, general work capacity
cue: Chest up, shoulders back, brace the core like you're bracing for a hit — walk tall and don't let the weight round your shoulders forward.

primary_purpose: Advanced anti-extension/hip flexor core strength
cue: Hang tall, brace the ribs down, and curl the hips up toward you — this is a core exercise, not a hip flexor swinging contest, so control the tempo.

primary_purpose: Vertical power for layout, blocks, contested catches
cue: Load quick, swing the arms, and explode up onto the box — land soft with the knees bent, don't just jump up and let it slam.

primary_purpose: Reflexive strength per Garage Strength's progression
cue: Step off, don't jump off — land, and the instant your feet touch, explode back up as fast as you can. Ground contact should be quick, not a pause.

primary_purpose: Frontal-plane power for cutting and marking
cue: Load and push off one leg, land soft and stuck on the other — stick the landing before you bound back the other way.

primary_purpose: Unilateral reactive strength; transfers to single-leg takeoffs for layout/blocks
cue: Load on one leg, drive up or out explosively, and land under control — balance the landing before you reset for the next rep.

primary_purpose: Reactive strength; rhythm and ground-contact time development
cue: Quick ground contacts — think 'hot coals,' minimal time on the floor between hurdles. Stay tall, don't collapse at the knees.

primary_purpose: Horizontal power for layout distance and acceleration
cue: Load the hips back, swing the arms hard, and jump for maximum distance — land soft with the knees bent and stick it.

primary_purpose: Upper-body explosive power; full-body deceleration/reset pattern
cue: Reach the ball high overhead, then whip it down into the ground as hard as you can, using your whole body, not just your arms.

primary_purpose: Upper-body explosive pressing power
cue: Load into the chest, then punch the ball straight out explosively — this should feel like you're pushing someone off of you.

primary_purpose: Tendon-pain regression entry point
cue: Hold position, brace, steady breathing.

exercise_name: Acceleration Mechanics Drill (e.g., wall drill, falling starts)
primary_purpose: Deep-cut sprinting demand
cue: Stay low, drive the knees forward and down hard, and keep your shin angle consistent — this is about building the pattern before we ever add speed.

primary_purpose: Full-speed sprinting demand
cue: Tall posture, quick ground contacts, and relaxed shoulders — sprinting fast is as much about staying loose as it is about pushing hard.

primary_purpose: Knee drive and ground-contact patterning
cue: Drive the knee up to hip height, punch it down actively into the ground — quick and rhythmic, not a slow high-knee march.

primary_purpose: Hamstring/leg-cycling patterning
cue: Same knee drive as an A-skip, but now extend the leg out in front before punching it down — stay tall and rhythmic.

primary_purpose: Acceleration mechanics; teaches forward lean and shin angle at the start
cue: Start tall, fall forward until you have to catch yourself, then drive out low and hard — let gravity start you, then attack.

primary_purpose: Acceleration-specific overload; force production in the drive phase
cue: Stay low, drive hard through the ground, and keep the shin angle aggressive the whole way — the sled should never pull you upright early.

primary_purpose: Top-end/max-velocity mechanics
cue: Build into your top speed gradually before the marked zone, then relax and let your legs turn over fast — trying to force speed usually slows you down.

primary_purpose: Acceleration mechanics from a game-realistic starting position (deep-cut starts)
cue: Explosive first step, low shin angle, and drive — don't pop straight up out of the start, stay low and build.

primary_purpose: Landing/deceleration mechanics for layout and cutting
cue: Land soft with bent knees and hips back, like you're sitting into a chair — absorb the landing before you do anything else with it.

primary_purpose: Multidirectional change-of-direction and deceleration under game-like demand
cue: Stay low through the whole shuttle, plant hard, and redirect explosively — the change of direction is where the drill is won or lost, not the straight-ahead speed.

primary_purpose: Sport-specific cutting mechanics
cue: Decelerate under control before the cut — plant the outside foot and drive out hard in the new direction, staying low through the whole change.

primary_purpose: Footwork and coordination; warm-up or technical emphasis
cue: Stay light and quick on your feet — eyes up, not down at the cones. Quality of movement over speed until the pattern is clean.

exercise_name: Hip Mobility Drill (deep lunge / 90-90 or similar)
primary_purpose: Deep lunge and lateral hip mobility for throwing/marking (Sec. 3)
cue: Move into the position slow and controlled, breathe into the stretch, and only go as deep as you can control — mobility work isn't about forcing range.

primary_purpose: Isolated hamstring strength; injury-prevention accessory for hamstring strain risk (Sec. 3)
cue: Control the weight down just as much as you curl it up — squeeze the hamstring hard at the top, don't let your hips come off the pad.

primary_purpose: Isolated hamstring strength; equipment variation
cue: Same idea seated — curl the heels toward you under control, squeeze at the top, and resist the weight back down slowly.

primary_purpose: Eccentric hamstring strength; strong evidence-based injury-prevention exercise for sprinting sports
cue: Lower yourself forward as slow as you possibly can, resisting with the hamstrings the entire way — catch yourself with your hands only at the very end.

primary_purpose: Bodyweight, equipment-limited hamstring isolation
cue: Brace the hips up and curl the heels in under you — keep the hips high the whole set, don't let them sag toward the floor.

primary_purpose: Isolated quad strength; knee extensor capacity
cue: Extend the knee under control and squeeze the quad hard at the top — control the weight back down, don't let it drop.

primary_purpose: Bodyweight/weighted quad isolation, no-machine option
cue: Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders and lean back slowly, using the quads to control the descent — this is a controlled lean, not a fall.

primary_purpose: Quad isolation under sustained tension; commonly used for patellar tendon loading
cue: Lean back into the band, sit into a wall-sit position, and hold — you should feel this burning through the front of the thigh, not the knees.

primary_purpose: Isometric quad endurance; tendon-pain-friendly entry point
cue: Back flat against the wall, thighs parallel to the ground — hold steady and breathe through it, don't hold your breath and grind.

primary_purpose: Gastrocnemius-biased calf strength
cue: Rise up onto your toes as high as you can, pause, then lower slow and controlled through a full range — don't bounce at the bottom.

primary_purpose: Soleus-biased calf strength; relevant to Achilles tendon health (Sec. 3)
cue: Same calf raise, seated this time to bias the lower calf — full range, controlled tempo, pause at the top.

primary_purpose: Equipment-limited, unilateral calf strength
cue: One leg at a time — rise up slow, control the lowering even slower. If you're wobbling all over, slow down further.

primary_purpose: Eccentric-emphasis calf loading; standard Achilles tendinopathy rehab/prevention exercise
cue: Rise up with both feet, then shift all your weight to one leg and lower yourself down as slowly as you can — this eccentric lowering is where the tendon actually adapts.

primary_purpose: Hip flexor strength; supports knee-drive in sprint mechanics
cue: Brace the core so you're not just rocking your whole body — drive the knee up against the band under control.

primary_purpose: Hip flexor isolation and control; no-equipment option
cue: Slow and controlled, drive the knee up and lower it back down without letting your low back arch to help.

primary_purpose: Hip flexor and lower-ab strength under load
cue: Hang tall, brace the ribs down, and curl the knees up toward your chest under control — no swinging.

primary_purpose: Adductor strength; strong evidence-based injury-prevention exercise for groin strain risk (Sec. 3)
cue: Brace the side plank position, then squeeze the ball or bench between your legs as hard as you can and hold — the top knee should barely move.

primary_purpose: Isolated adductor strength; groin strain prevention accessory
cue: Squeeze the inner thigh to pull the cable across your body — control it back out slowly, don't let the weight yank you.

primary_purpose: Machine-based adductor isolation; equipment-limited alternative
cue: Squeeze your inner thighs together against the pads — full range, controlled tempo, no bouncing the weight.

primary_purpose: Glute isolation and activation; entry point to hip thrust pattern
cue: Squeeze the glutes hard at the top like you're trying to crack a walnut between your cheeks — control the way back down.

primary_purpose: Glute-dominant hip extension power; force production relevant to sprint/jump output
cue: Drive through your heels and squeeze the glutes hard at the top — this should be a glute exercise, not a low-back exercise, so keep the ribs down.

primary_purpose: Isolated glute max strength
cue: Squeeze the glute to kick the leg back and slightly up — control the return, don't let the band just snap it back.

primary_purpose: Glute medius isolation; hip stability relevant to knee-valgus control on cutting/landing
cue: Keep your feet together and heels touching, then open the top knee using just the glute — don't let your hips roll back to fake the range.

primary_purpose: Glute medius strength and hip stability for cutting and marking
cue: Stay in a slight squat the whole time, and step sideways under tension — small, controlled steps, keep the band tight throughout.

primary_purpose: Rotator cuff strength; shoulder health for throwing volume (Sec. 3)
cue: Elbow tucked to your side, rotate the forearm out against the resistance — small range, but control it fully, don't let the band snap you back.

primary_purpose: Rotator cuff strength; shoulder health for throwing volume
cue: Same setup, rotating the forearm in this time — slow and controlled, this is about the small stabilizer muscles, not swinging weight around.

primary_purpose: Classic isolated rotator cuff strengthening
cue: Lying on your side, elbow tucked, rotate the dumbbell up under control — keep the elbow pinned to your side the whole rep.

primary_purpose: Scapular stability and rotator cuff endurance; shoulder health for throwing volume
cue: Move slow through each letter position, squeezing the shoulder blades together — light weight, full control, this is about quality of movement.

primary_purpose: Shoulder/rotator cuff health; supraspinatus emphasis
cue: Raise the arm up and out at an angle, thumb slightly up, to about shoulder height — control it back down, don't use momentum.

primary_purpose: General arm accessory strength
cue: Elbows pinned to your sides, curl the weight up under control without swinging your body to help.

primary_purpose: Forearm/brachialis accessory strength
cue: Same curl, neutral grip this time — control it up and down, elbows stay locked at your sides.

primary_purpose: General arm accessory strength
cue: Elbows pinned at your sides, extend the arms down fully and squeeze the triceps at the bottom — control the weight back up.

primary_purpose: General arm accessory strength
cue: Keep the elbows pointed forward and close to your head, extend the arm fully overhead and control it back down.

primary_purpose: Spinal erector strength; supports repeated rotational throwing/diving demand (Sec. 3)
cue: Hinge from the hips, keep a flat back, and extend up until your body is in a straight line — don't hyperextend past neutral at the top.

primary_purpose: Posterior chain/lower-back strength with less spinal compression
cue: Hinge from the hips, then squeeze the glutes to lift the legs — this is a glute and hamstring exercise, so don't let the low back do the lifting.

primary_purpose: Forearm/wrist strength relevant to disc grip and snap on release
cue: Palm up, curl the wrist toward you through a full range under control — this is a small muscle, so leave the ego at the door.

primary_purpose: Wrist extensor strength; balances flexor-dominant throwing demand
cue: Palm down this time, curl the wrist up under control — full range, slow tempo.

primary_purpose: Sprint knee-drive patterning without needing distance to run
cue: Quick, light contacts — drive the knees up fast without traveling forward. This is about rhythm and turnover, not distance.

primary_purpose: Ground-contact speed and rhythm in a small footprint
cue: Stay light on your toes and move the feet as fast as you can — quick and controlled, not sloppy and out of control.

primary_purpose: Acceleration drive-phase mechanics without needing sprint distance
cue: Drive the knee up against the band resistance, then punch it down actively — this builds the same pattern as sprinting, just with extra load to make it stick.

primary_purpose: Acceleration mechanics for athletes without a full sprint runway
cue: Start low and build your speed gradually over the distance — this is about the acceleration pattern, not seeing how fast you can go in the first two steps.

primary_purpose: Vertical power development without needing running distance
cue: Sit back into a quarter squat, then explode straight up as high as you can. Land soft, reset, and go again — quality reps only.

primary_purpose: Vertical power and hip-flexor-driven jump mechanics in a small footprint
cue: Jump straight up and pull the knees to your chest fast, then land soft and immediately reset for the next one.

primary_purpose: Lateral power for cutting, trainable without running room
cue: Push off one leg laterally, land soft on the other, and stick it for a beat before bounding back the other way — control over speed early on.

primary_purpose: General vertical power assessment/training in minimal floor space
cue: Dip quick, swing the arms up, and jump as high as you can — this measures how well you use the stretch-shortening cycle, so make the dip quick, not slow.

primary_purpose: Defensive lateral movement mechanics in a small footprint
cue: Stay low, feet don't cross, and push off the trail leg hard to move — quick, athletic shuffles, not a slow side-step.

primary_purpose: Reflexive/reactive ankle strength using minimal jump height
cue: Small, quick hops — stiff ankles, minimal knee bend. Think of a pogo stick, not a squat jump.

primary_purpose: Bodyweight vertical-pressing substitute that doesn't require overhead bar path clearance
cue: Hips high, hands under the shoulders — lower the head toward the ground between your hands and press back up. Think of it as a stepping stone to a handstand push-up.

primary_purpose: Advanced bodyweight overhead-pressing progression
cue: Brace hard, lower under control until the head lightly touches, then press back up through a full lockout. Control beats speed here — no crashing down.

primary_purpose: High-intensity conditioning with no overhead movement and a small footprint
cue: Grip the ropes, get in an athletic stance, and go all-out — big, aggressive waves the whole interval, not a wristy flick.

primary_purpose: No-equipment hinge-pattern competency and coaching entry point
cue: Hold the dowel against your head, low back, and tailbone — hinge back at the hips while keeping all three points of contact. If the dowel comes off your back, you're rounding.

primary_purpose: No-equipment single-leg strength and mobility
cue: Big step, soft landing, knee stacked over the ankle. Drive through the front heel to come back up — own the balance the whole way.

primary_purpose: Single-leg strength progression; equipment-optional (bench for rear foot)
cue: Back foot up, weight in the front heel. Sit straight down like there's a wall behind you, then drive the floor away to stand back up.

primary_purpose: Single-leg strength using minimal equipment (box or stair)
cue: Drive through the working leg's whole foot — don't push off the back leg to cheat the rep. Stand tall at the top, control the way back down.

primary_purpose: No-equipment unilateral glute strength progression
cue: One leg planted, squeeze the glute hard at the top and hold for a beat — keep the hips level, don't let one side dip.

primary_purpose: No-equipment lower-back and anti-extension/anti-rotation combination
cue: Reach opposite arm and leg out long, keep the low back flat and the core braced — this is about stability, not how far you can reach.

primary_purpose: No-equipment full-body core and shoulder stability under load
cue: Hips low, back flat like a tabletop, and move opposite hand and foot together under control. Stay braced the whole way — don't let the hips bounce.

primary_purpose: No-equipment core and conditioning combination movement
cue: Hold a strong plank position and drive the knees in quick, under control — hips stay level, don't let them pike up into the air.

primary_purpose: No-equipment horizontal pulling substitute using a doorframe or towel anchor
cue: Row yourself up and toward the anchor, body straight, chest driving to the target. Control the lowering — that's where the work happens.

primary_purpose: Phosphagen-system development; top-speed and acceleration power with full recovery
cue: Full sprint, every rep — if you're not close to max effort, you're not training the quality this is meant for. Walk back, fully recover, go again.

primary_purpose: Phosphagen-system development with added resistance
cue: Stay low and drive hard the entire distance — this should be all-out, so pick a load you can still sprint against, not just drag.

exercise_name: Assault Bike Sprint Intervals (10-15s Max Effort)
primary_purpose: Phosphagen-system development without needing running room
cue: All-out effort for the work interval — if you can hold a conversation during it, it's not hard enough. Full recovery between rounds.

primary_purpose: Indoor, minimal-space alternative to running-based speed work
cue: Max effort on the work intervals — stand up out of the saddle if you need to, this should feel like a sprint on two wheels.

primary_purpose: Anaerobic-glycolytic capacity; directly matches 30-90s point-length demand (Sec. 3)
cue: Aggressive but controlled pace — this should hurt by the last 50 meters, but you shouldn't fall apart mechanically. Hold your form.

primary_purpose: Anaerobic capacity with direction changes; sport-relevant conditioning
cue: Hard, sustained effort with a defined work-to-rest ratio — this is about repeating quality efforts, not just surviving one.

primary_purpose: Anaerobic capacity without needing running room; matches point-length demand
cue: Hard, sustained push for the work interval, then truly rest during the rest — don't half-effort the work or half-rest the recovery.

primary_purpose: Anaerobic capacity and footwork rhythm in a small footprint
cue: Stay light on your feet, relaxed shoulders, and keep a consistent rhythm — this is as much about coordination as conditioning.

primary_purpose: Anaerobic capacity without needing running room; low-impact
cue: Legs drive first, then lean, then pull — in that order, every stroke. Don't just yank with your arms.

primary_purpose: Anaerobic capacity with upper-body/full-body emphasis; low-impact alternative
cue: Full-body effort — legs, hips, and arms working together on every pull. Stay aggressive through the whole interval.

exercise_name: Bodyweight Conditioning Circuit (burpees, mountain climbers, high knees)
primary_purpose: Anaerobic conditioning with zero equipment and minimal space
cue: Move with intent through each exercise — this is conditioning, not a form check, but don't let your technique fall apart just to go faster.

primary_purpose: Aerobic power development and recovery-between-efforts capacity
cue: Comfortably hard — you should be working, but able to hold your pace and form the entire distance. This isn't a sprint.

primary_purpose: Aerobic base; supports repeat-effort capacity across a tournament weekend (Sec. 3)
cue: Settle into a pace you could sustain the whole time — steady effort, steady breathing, this is about building your aerobic engine, not testing your max.

exercise_name: Repeated Sprint Ability Series (6-10 x 20-30 yd, 20-30s Rest)
primary_purpose: Directly matches point length and tournament repeat-effort demand (Sec. 3) — the most sport-specific conditioning tool in this library
cue: Every sprint at max effort, every rest period respected — this only works if the sprints stay fast, so don't let fatigue turn it into a jog.

primary_purpose: Sport-specific repeated-effort conditioning under game-realistic decision-making
cue: Play with intent — this is conditioning through the actual demands of the game, so move like you would in a real point.

exercise_name: Assault Bike Repeated-Effort Intervals (game-length work:rest ratio)
primary_purpose: Repeated-sprint-ability training without needing field/running room
cue: Match the work-to-rest ratio to what you'd actually see in a point and recovery — go hard when it's go time, actually rest when it's rest time.

primary_purpose: Quad/patellar tendon isometric loading at mid-range knee flexion
cue: Set the knee at the target angle and push into the pad without moving — steady, even tension for the full hold, breathe through it.

primary_purpose: Hamstring isometric strength at a vulnerable mid-range joint angle
cue: Set up at the sticking point of your Nordic and hold there, fighting to stay upright — don't let yourself collapse forward.

primary_purpose: Static adductor strength; classic groin-strain rehab/prevention isometric
cue: Squeeze the ball or bench between your knees as hard as you can and hold — steady pressure the whole time, not a series of pulses.

primary_purpose: Static adductor strength at end-range
cue: Set up at the top of the Copenhagen position and hold — brace the whole body, this should feel like a full-body plank with extra adductor demand.

exercise_name: Isometric Calf Raise Hold (Mid-Range, Straight Knee)
primary_purpose: Gastrocnemius/Achilles tendon isometric loading
cue: Rise up onto your toes to the target height and hold there — steady, even tension, don't let yourself sink down early.

exercise_name: Isometric Calf Raise Hold (Bent Knee, Soleus-Biased)
primary_purpose: Soleus/Achilles isometric loading
cue: Same hold, knee bent this time to bias the lower calf — hold steady and breathe.

primary_purpose: Proprioception and ankle stability
cue: Stand tall on one leg and hold — small adjustments are fine, but don't let your hips or shoulders sway around.

primary_purpose: Rotator cuff isometric strength at a throwing-relevant joint angle
cue: Elbow at 90 degrees, push your hand into the resistance without moving — steady, even pressure the whole hold.

primary_purpose: Shoulder/scapular stability under isometric load
cue: Hold a strong push-up position and brace like you're about to get pushed — no sagging, no piking, just a rock-solid hold.

exercise_name: Isometric Back Extension Hold (Prone or Hyper Bench)
primary_purpose: Spinal erector isometric endurance
cue: Lift into the extended position and hold — brace the glutes and low back together, steady breathing throughout.

primary_purpose: Max-effort (~3-5s) isometric to build tendon stiffness and rate of force development
cue: Set the bar at the target position and pull against it as hard as you can — this is a true max-effort push, drive through the floor like you're trying to rip the bar off the pins.
contrast_pairing_tendon_specific: PJ-012 (Countermovement Jump) or PJ-002 (Depth Jump) — hold max effort, then perform the jump within seconds

primary_purpose: Max-effort isometric squat at a joint angle relevant to sprint/jump mechanics
cue: Set up in the squat position against the pins and push up into them as hard as you can — full-body tension, breathe and brace, then attack it.
contrast_pairing_tendon_specific: PJ-001 (Box Jump) or PJ-009 (Squat Jump) — hold max effort, then perform the jump within seconds

exercise_name: Max Isometric Split Squat Hold (Front Knee)
primary_purpose: Max-effort unilateral isometric for tendon stiffness relevant to single-leg takeoffs
cue: Front knee set at the target angle, push down into the ground as hard as you can through that front leg and hold.
contrast_pairing_tendon_specific: PJ-017 (Single-Leg Hop and Stick) or PJ-016 (Single-Leg Hop for Distance)

primary_purpose: Max-effort Achilles tendon stiffness development
cue: Load up and rise onto your toes into the pins, pushing up as hard as you can — max effort, short duration, then rest.
contrast_pairing_tendon_specific: PJ-013 (Low-Amplitude Pogo Hop) or PJ-019 (Repeated Single-Leg Ankle Hops)

primary_purpose: Max-effort glute/proximal-hamstring tendon stiffness; force production relevant to sprint drive phase
cue: Drive your hips up into the bar as hard as you can and hold — squeeze everything, this is a max-effort push, not a slow burn.

primary_purpose: Max-effort upper-back/shoulder tendon stiffness, throwing-adjacent
cue: Row into the resistance as hard as you can and hold — full tension through the back and arms, short and maximal.
contrast_pairing_tendon_specific: PJ-008 (Medicine Ball Chest Pass) or an explosive upper-body throw of the coach's choice (cross-pattern pairing)

primary_purpose: Ankle stiffness/reactive strength with minimal knee involvement
cue: Stay tall through the hips and drive the pop through your ankle, not your knee — quick, springy contacts.

primary_purpose: Frontal-plane single-leg power relevant to cutting and marking
cue: Push off one leg sideways, land on the other and stick it, then push right back — stay light and quick on your feet.

primary_purpose: Single-leg horizontal power assessment/training
cue: Load the hips, swing the arms, and hop for maximum distance on one leg — stick the landing balanced before you call the rep done.

primary_purpose: Single-leg landing control; ACL/ankle injury-prevention relevant
cue: Hop out and land on one leg — the moment your foot touches, freeze and hold it. If you wobble or need a second hop to balance, that's the rep giving you feedback.

primary_purpose: Single-leg vertical power with a landing target
cue: Load on one leg, hop up onto the box, and land soft and balanced — this is about control on a single leg, not just getting up there.

primary_purpose: Ankle reactive strength/health via repeated ground contacts
cue: Quick, stiff-ankle hops in place on one leg — minimal time on the ground, like the floor is hot.

primary_purpose: Lateral single-leg power combined with landing control, cutting-relevant
cue: Push off one leg into a lateral hop, land on the other, and hold it stuck for a full second before you go again.

primary_purpose: Dynamic internal/external hip rotation; directly supports deep lunge and lateral lunge demand for throwing/marking (Sec. 3)
cue: Move slow and controlled between positions — this is about active control through the range, not just stretching passively.

primary_purpose: Active hip joint mobility and control through full range
cue: Move through the full circle slow and controlled — if you feel a pinch or have to compensate, that's the edge of your range for today.

primary_purpose: Static/dynamic deep lunge position mobility for throwing mechanics and marking
cue: Sink into the lunge, then rotate toward your front leg and reach tall — breathe into the stretch rather than forcing it deeper.

primary_purpose: Dynamic lateral lunge mobility; directly ties to marking and lateral hip demand (Sec. 3)
cue: Shift your weight side to side slow and controlled, sitting deep into each hip — keep your chest up and both feet flat as long as you can.

primary_purpose: Hip flexor mobility; supports full-speed sprinting mechanics (hip extension range, Sec. 3)
cue: Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck the hips under — you should feel this in the front of the hip, not your low back.

primary_purpose: Adductor/groin mobility; complements groin-strain prevention isometrics
cue: Sink your hips down and back slowly, breathing into the stretch — this should feel like a deep, calm opening through the groin, not a fight.

exercise_name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch with Reach
primary_purpose: Hip flexor mobility with an added thoracic extension/reach component
cue: Tuck the back hip under, squeeze the glute, and reach the same-side arm up and over — you're stretching the hip flexor, not arching your low back.

primary_purpose: Combined hip and thoracic mobility; common dynamic warm-up staple
cue: Drop into a deep lunge, then rotate open toward your front leg, reaching your arm up toward the ceiling.

primary_purpose: Glute/hip external rotation mobility
cue: Stand tall, cross one ankle over the opposite knee, and sit your hips back slowly — keep your back flat, not rounded.

primary_purpose: Single-leg dynamic hip control and mobility, balance-integrated
cue: Balance on one leg and rotate the other hip open and closed slow and controlled — this is about active control, not momentum.

primary_purpose: Combined hip/ankle mobility at end-range squat depth
cue: Sink down as deep as you can with your heels flat and chest tall — hang out here and breathe, let gravity do the work.

primary_purpose: Dynamic groin/hip mobility with a reaching component; warm-up friendly
cue: Sit back into one hip, keep the other leg long and straight, and reach both hands toward your front foot.

primary_purpose: Lying hip internal/external rotation mobility; low-impact entry point
cue: Lying down, knees bent, let them fall slowly side to side under control — keep your shoulders flat on the ground the whole time.

primary_purpose: Static glute/hip external rotation stretch
cue: Settle into the position slow, square your hips as best you can, and breathe into the stretch through the glute.

primary_purpose: Ankle dorsiflexion range; supports squat depth and landing mechanics
cue: Keep your heel flat on the ground and drive the knee toward the wall — if the heel lifts, you've gone too far, back off.

primary_purpose: Active ankle joint mobility and control through full range
cue: Move the ankle through its full range slow and controlled — point, flex, and circle, feeling for any restricted spots.

primary_purpose: Joint-focused ankle mobility work for deeper dorsiflexion range
cue: Let the band pull the joint gently while you move the ankle through its range — this should feel like more room, not pain.

primary_purpose: Loaded dorsiflexion mobility; supports deceleration and landing mechanics
cue: Keep the heel down and rock the knee forward over the toes slow and controlled — this builds the exact range you need for a deep squat.

primary_purpose: Gastrocnemius/Achilles mobility
cue: Keep the back knee straight and heel flat, then lean forward until you feel a stretch up through the calf — breathe into it.

primary_purpose: Soleus/Achilles mobility
cue: Bend the back knee this time and sink the hips down — you're targeting deeper into the calf than the straight-knee version.

primary_purpose: Active mobility and proprioception; useful post-ankle-sprain
cue: Trace the alphabet slowly with your foot in the air — this is about control through full range, not speed.

primary_purpose: Dynamic dorsiflexion mobility integrated into a half-kneeling position
cue: Half-kneeling with the foot flat, rock the knee forward over the toes — keep the heel glued to the ground the whole time.

primary_purpose: Active shoulder joint mobility and control through full range
cue: Move the shoulder through its full circle slow and controlled — feel for where the range gets tight and work that spot a little longer.

primary_purpose: Scapular control and overhead shoulder mobility
cue: Back flat against the wall, slide the arms up and down while keeping contact — if your low back arches off the wall, you've found your limit for today.

primary_purpose: Posterior shoulder/internal rotation mobility; addresses GIRD common in throwing athletes
cue: Settle into the position and let the shoulder relax into the stretch — this one should feel like a deep, calm opening in the back of the shoulder.

primary_purpose: Posterior capsule mobility
cue: Pull the arm gently across your body and hold — breathe into it, don't yank or bounce.

primary_purpose: Throwing-specific external rotation mobility
cue: Rotate the arm slowly through its range at 90 degrees — stop right where you feel the stretch, don't force past it.

primary_purpose: Anterior shoulder/chest mobility; supports throwing posture and overhead positions
cue: Lean gently into the doorway with the arm at shoulder height, feeling the stretch across the front of the chest — breathe and relax into it.

primary_purpose: Dynamic shoulder mobility combined with scapular activation
cue: Pull the band apart while reaching overhead — combine the upper back squeeze with some shoulder mobility in one move.

primary_purpose: Dynamic shoulder mobility; warm-up staple
cue: Big, slow, controlled circles — this is a warm-up mobility drill, not a race, so keep the range full and the tempo easy.

primary_purpose: Thoracic rotational mobility; directly supports rotational throwing power and control (Sec. 3)
cue: Start on all fours, thread one arm under and through, rotating through the upper back — keep the hips still so the rotation comes from your spine.

primary_purpose: Thoracic rotational mobility, side-lying variation
cue: Lying on your side, open the top arm like you're opening a book, following it with your eyes — let the upper back rotate, not just the arm.

primary_purpose: Dynamic thoracic rotation; warm-up friendly, throwing-relevant
cue: Stand tall, rotate through the upper back and reach one arm around behind you — keep your hips facing forward the whole time.

primary_purpose: Advanced absolute lower-body strength with a more upright torso position; carries over well from Olympic lift catch positions
cue: Elbows up, bar resting on the front of the shoulders — stay tall through the torso as you sit down, don't let the elbows drop or the bar will roll.

primary_purpose: Advanced posterior chain strength; highest absolute-load hinge variation
cue: Set your hips back, flat back, bar tight to your shins — drive through the floor and stand tall, don't let the bar drift away from your body.

primary_purpose: Loaded/resisted progression of thoracic rotational mobility; bridges mobility work toward rotational power development
cue: Half-kneeling, band anchored to the side — rotate through the upper back against the resistance, keeping the hips square the whole time.

primary_purpose: Anti-rotation core control from a more challenging, less stable base than standing
cue: Half-kneeling so you can't cheat with your hips — press the band straight out and hold, resisting any rotation through the torso.

primary_purpose: Anti-rotation core control combined with single-leg hip drive; higher carryover to cutting/marking
cue: Press the band out and hold your center, then march in place without letting your torso twist toward the band. Slow and controlled beats fast and sloppy.

primary_purpose: Anti-rotation core stability under an alternating loaded-pull demand
cue: Brace hard in a strong plank, then row one hand at a time without letting your hips rock side to side. If your hips are swinging, slow down.

primary_purpose: Combined anti-rotation/anti-extension core stability under a moving base
cue: Find a strong plank on the ball, then make small controlled circles or figure-eights — brace so the ball moves, not your spine.

primary_purpose: Anti-rotation control against a resisted chopping motion
cue: Start with the cable at your shoulder or hip, then chop across your body while keeping your hips and shoulders square — this is about resisting rotation, not creating it.

primary_purpose: Combined anti-rotation/anti-extension core stability using bodyweight and instability
cue: Set your feet, lean forward into the straps, and pull yourself back to center while keeping the hips square — resist the fall, don't just muscle through it.

primary_purpose: Loaded progression of the bodyweight Bird Dog; anti-rotation under added resistance
cue: Same bird dog setup, now fighting a band trying to pull you off — brace hard and move slow, this is a stability drill, not a strength one.

primary_purpose: Rotational power with a lateral hip-drive emphasis; transfers to throwing off the back foot
cue: Rotate and load into your back hip like you're winding up, then whip the ball out to the side with your hips leading the throw.

primary_purpose: Rotational power development using constant-tension resistance rather than a thrown implement
cue: Set your feet, rotate away from the cable to load, then throw your hips and torso through together — this should feel like a disc throw, not just an arm swing.

primary_purpose: Full-body rotational power combining hip and trunk rotation under load
cue: Rotate through the hips first, torso follows — this is the same sequencing as a big throw, so make it feel athletic, not robotic.

primary_purpose: Explosive rotational power in a downward diagonal chop-slam pattern
cue: Load by rotating away from the target, then slam the ball down and across explosively — hips lead, arms finish.

primary_purpose: Rotational power in the downward diagonal pattern
cue: Start high, finish low, and let the rotation come from your hips and torso together — the cable should never pull you off balance.

primary_purpose: Rotational power in the upward diagonal pattern
cue: Start low, finish high, driving up through the back leg and hips — think of it as an uppercut for your whole body.

primary_purpose: Full-body rotational power expressed explosively through the lower body and trunk together
cue: Load, rotate, and land the jump stuck and balanced — the whole point of this one is control on the landing, not just the spin.

primary_purpose: Entry-level rotational endurance/power; accessible progression before loaded throws
cue: Sit back slightly, brace the core, and rotate side to side under control — this is about a strong midline, not how fast you can swing.

primary_purpose: Single-leg strength staple; high carryover to cutting, marking, and single-leg force production
cue: Back foot elevated, most of your weight in the front heel. Sit straight down between hip and knee, then push the ground away — this one should feel like a squat on one leg, not a lunge.

primary_purpose: Classic barbell hinge strength and hamstring loading; the standard RDL
cue: Push your hips back first, soft bend in the knees, bar tight to your legs the whole way down — feel the stretch in the hamstrings, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.

exercise_name: Dead Bug with Plate Pass (Dying Bug Plate Pass)
primary_purpose: Anti-extension core control with an added overhead plate-pass challenge; progression from the basic Dead Bug
cue: Flatten your low back into the floor and keep it there the whole rep — pass the plate overhead slow and controlled, brace like someone's about to press on your stomach.

primary_purpose: Advanced single-leg squat strength, balance, and control; high single-leg force demand relevant to layout and single-leg landing mechanics
cue: This is a control exercise before it's a strength exercise — sit back slow, chest tall, and own the bottom before you ever try to stand back up fast.

primary_purpose: Upper body explosive power and rate of force development off the ground — directly relevant to layout recovery, contact absorption/re-push, and upper-body power transfer in throwing
cue: Set up in a push-up, brace hard, and push yourself explosively off the ground — land soft with a slight bend in the elbows to absorb it.

primary_purpose: Higher-intensity progression of the plyo push-up using a slight drop to increase eccentric loading before the explosive push
cue: Small drop off the boxes, then land and immediately explode back up onto the next set — this is a higher gear than the standard plyo push-up, so respect the intensity.

exercise_name: Medicine Ball Explosive Chest Pass (Standing, Max Effort)
primary_purpose: Horizontal upper-body power expression against an external implement — mirrors the push/re-push demand of contesting a disc or recovering from contact
cue: Load into your chest and hips together, then throw the ball as hard and as far as you can — full extension, full commitment.

primary_purpose: Single-arm rotational upper-body power, closer to the unilateral, rotational force production pattern of a disc throw than a bilateral chest pass
cue: Rotate and load through the back hip, then explode the ball out to the side like you're putting a shot — hips lead, arm finishes.

primary_purpose: Adds a lateral/reactive element to the plyo push-up for athletes needing off-axis upper-body power and control, closer to a layout-recovery demand
cue: Push off explosively and reach one hand out to the side as you land, catching your weight under control — this is about power and control together.

primary_purpose: Accommodating-resistance variation that overloads the top/lockout portion of the push-up, building explosive intent without needing a true plyo landing — a good bridge for athletes not yet ready for full plyo push-ups
cue: Same push-up setup, but attack the top half — once the band gets tight, drive through it fast. This is where we build the explosive push-up pattern before we ever leave the ground.

primary_purpose: Accessible, no-equipment quad/knee isometric tolerance builder — good early-stage option for reactive knee pain or a novice athlete's first isometric exposure
cue: Back flat against the wall, thighs parallel — hold steady, breathe, and don't let your knees cave in toward each other.

primary_purpose: Single-leg progression of the knee/ACL isometric series — adds a unilateral loading and balance demand once bilateral holds are well tolerated
cue: Set the front knee at the target angle and hold — steady pressure through the front foot, this one tests your balance as much as your strength.

primary_purpose: Bilateral hip-extension isometric hold that loads the hamstring at a longer muscle length than the Nordic hold — a gentler regression option for reactive hamstring pain
cue: Bridge up and hold at the top, squeezing the hamstrings and glutes together — steady tension, no shaking it out early.

primary_purpose: Single-leg hip-hinge isometric hold — combines hamstring isometric loading with the balance and posterior-chain control needed for sprinting and cutting
cue: Balance on one leg, hinge forward to the target position, and hold — steady and controlled, this is as much about balance as strength.

primary_purpose: Sustained top-range calf isometric — early-stage loading option for reactive Achilles/ankle pain before slow-resistance or hopping work is reintroduced
cue: Rise up onto your toes to the top and just hold there — steady tension, breathe through it, don't let yourself sink.

exercise_name: Isometric Single-Leg Balance Hold with Perturbation
primary_purpose: Progression of the basic single-leg balance hold — adds an external perturbation (partner push, ball toss) to build reactive ankle stability closer to game demands
cue: Stand tall on one leg and hold your position through the push or the toss — react quick, then reset and stay tall.

primary_purpose: Low-load anti-extension/anti-rotation hold for the lower back and hips — a gentle, accessible entry point for athletes managing lower back irritation
cue: Reach opposite arm and leg out and hold — brace the core so your low back doesn't sag, steady breathing the whole time.

primary_purpose: Prone lower-back and posterior-chain isometric hold — targets extensor endurance relevant to repeated throwing and diving demands
cue: Lift chest and legs off the ground together and hold — squeeze the glutes and low back, steady tension, don't strain the neck.

primary_purpose: Progression of the basic side plank — adds a top-leg abduction movement that increases the anti-lateral-flexion demand and adds a hip-strength component relevant to cutting
cue: Same strong side plank, now lift the top leg without letting your hips drop or rotate back — this should feel like your hip is doing the work, not your shoulder.

primary_purpose: Standing/half-kneeling resisted anti-lateral flexion — trains the same quality as the side plank in a more upright, sport-relevant position
cue: Half-kneeling, band pulling you sideways — brace and resist it, don't let your ribs cave toward the band.

primary_purpose: Static anti-lateral-flexion hold with an offset load — distinct from the Suitcase Carry (Core - Loaded Carry) in that the athlete holds rather than walks, isolating the anti-lateral-flexion demand
cue: Stand tall, weight in one hand, and resist leaning toward it — brace like you're trying to stay perfectly upright with a heavy suitcase pulling you sideways.

primary_purpose: Advanced side plank variation adding a rotational reach-under — combines anti-lateral-flexion control with a controlled rotary component relevant to throwing and marking
cue: Hold the side plank strong, then reach the top arm underneath your body and back — control the rotation, don't let your hips drop while you reach.

primary_purpose: Lower-intensity entry point into reactive/reflexive strength work using a reduced drop height — appropriate before progressing to a full Depth Jump
cue: Step off a lower height, land, and pop right back up quick — this is the entry point, so focus on quick, light ground contact before we go higher.

primary_purpose: Higher-intensity reflexive-strength progression combining a depth drop with a maximal horizontal expression — appropriate only once the standard Depth Jump is well established
cue: Step off, land quick, and immediately convert straight into a max-effort broad jump — the depth jump primes you, the broad jump is where you show it.

primary_purpose: Shoulder- and wrist-friendly bar position for athletes with limited overhead/external shoulder mobility for a standard back squat, or as a substitution during a shoulder injury-return progression
cue: Bar sits high on your shoulders/traps instead of your back — stay tall through the torso and sit down the same way you would on a back squat. Should feel friendlier on the shoulders, not the legs.

primary_purpose: Single-implement squat variation for equipment-limited settings (garage/home gym) that still allows meaningful external load and is easier on the lower back and knees for less experienced lifters
cue: Hold the bar against your chest, brace hard, and sit down between your hips — the closer load in front changes your balance, so stay upright and own it.

primary_purpose: Unilateral hinge variation that builds hamstring strength and balance together and helps address side-to-side asymmetry — relevant given ultimate's single-leg cutting and landing demands
cue: Balance on one leg, hinge the hips back while your other leg reaches behind you for counterbalance — keep the hips square, don't let them rotate open.

primary_purpose: Explosive, ballistic hinge variation that trains hip-extension power in a repeatable, lower-skill-cost format than a barbell hinge — useful conditioning-adjacent power option
cue: Hike the bell back between your legs like a football snap, then snap the hips forward hard to float it up to chest height — the arms just guide it, the hips do the work.

primary_purpose: Triceps-emphasis bench variation, narrower grip shifts load off the pecs and onto the triceps/lockout strength — useful accessory for overhead and throwing power
cue: Hands just inside shoulder width, elbows tucked closer to the body than a regular bench — press straight up and really finish the lockout with the triceps.

primary_purpose: Limited-range bench-press variation performed on the floor — the floor stops the elbow past a certain depth, making it a shoulder-friendly pressing option and a good fit for a home/garage gym without a bench
cue: Elbows touch the floor lightly at the bottom — pause briefly, then press straight up without arching off the floor to cheat the range.

primary_purpose: Isolated rear-delt/upper-back work distinct from Face Pull and Band Pull-Apart — targets rear delt strength and posture specifically, useful high-volume accessory for shoulder health given throwing volume
cue: Hinge forward slightly, soft bend in the elbows, and raise the dumbbells out to the sides like you're spreading wings — squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, control it back down.

primary_purpose: Heavy, slow-tempo calf raise protocol (e.g., 3-4s up, 3-4s down) distinct from a standard calf raise — an evidence-based tendon-loading method for Achilles health and calf strength, especially useful during a reacclimation or return-to-training phase
cue: Load it heavier than you'd think and slow it way down — about a 3 count up and a 3 count down, no bouncing at the bottom or top.

primary_purpose: Machine/cable horizontal pull — the seated cable row you'd find in most commercial gyms; a stable, easy-to-load alternative to free-weight rows for athletes with cable access
cue: Sit tall, brace the core, and pull the handle to your stomach leading with the elbows — squeeze the shoulder blades together, control it back out without rounding forward.

primary_purpose: Unilateral cable row — adds an anti-rotation core demand on top of the pulling work since one side is loaded at a time
cue: Brace the core so your torso doesn't rotate with the pull — row the handle to your ribs, squeeze, control it back out.

primary_purpose: Standing cable press — the constant cable tension and standing position add a core-stability demand compared to a bench press, useful variety for athletes with cable access
cue: Split stance for a stable base, brace the core, and press straight out in front of you without letting your torso rotate.

primary_purpose: Isolated chest fly using cables — constant tension through the full range, a common accessory/pump exercise for athletes who have cable access
cue: Slight bend in the elbows, sweep the handles together in front of your chest like you're hugging a barrel — control the stretch back out.

primary_purpose: Cable upright row for shoulder/upper-trap work — a cable-specific variant for athletes who prefer the smoother resistance curve over a barbell version
cue: Pull the handle straight up close to your body, leading with the elbows — stop around chest height, don't force it higher than feels comfortable in the shoulder.

primary_purpose: Cable-based triceps isolation using a rope attachment — constant tension variant of an overhead triceps extension
cue: Elbows pointed forward and steady, extend your hands overhead and apart at the top, control it back down.

primary_purpose: Cable-based biceps curl — constant tension through the range compared to a free-weight curl
cue: Elbows pinned to your sides, curl the handle up under control without swinging your body to help.

primary_purpose: Cable-based lateral raise for the side delt — constant tension variant of a dumbbell lateral raise, useful shoulder-health accessory
cue: Raise the handle out to the side to about shoulder height, thumb slightly up — control it back down, don't use momentum.

primary_purpose: Cable-based rear delt isolation using crossed cables — a common cable-specific alternative to a dumbbell rear delt fly
cue: Cables crossed in front of you, sweep your arms out and back like you're opening curtains — squeeze the shoulder blades at the end.

primary_purpose: Cable-based hip hinge pattern — the cable resistance pulls from behind, which tends to teach the hip-hinge pattern (hips back, not squatting down) very cleanly for athletes still grooving the movement
cue: Hinge the hips back against the cable pulling from behind you, feel the stretch in the hamstrings, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.

primary_purpose: Combination cable squat-to-row movement pairing a lower-body pattern with a rowing pull — used as functional/conditioning-adjacent variety rather than a primary strength exercise
cue: Sit back into the squat, then stand and pull the handle to your ribs at the same time — one smooth motion, not two separate movements.
